# 大學疏義

**ID:** KR1h0029
**Custom ID:** ZB1h0025
**Source:** 四庫全書 文淵閣版, V202.1, p1
**Extent:** 1 卷

## Authors / Editors
- 金履祥 (宋朝) 撰 1232 - 1303

**Editions:** WYG

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 1-*juàn* sub-commentary on Zhū Xī's *Dàxué zhāngjù* and *Dàxué huòwèn* by Jīn Lǚxiáng — the leading Sòng-loyalist *Lǐxué* scholar of the late-13th and early-14th century, conventionally counted (with Wáng Bǎi 王柏 and Hé Jī 何基) among the **Zhèngjiào sān xiānshēng** 正教三先生 of the Jīnhuá / Wūzhōu (Zhū Xī southern lineage) school. Jīn Lǚxiáng paired this *Dàxué shūyì* with a parallel *zhǐyì* 指義 (one *piān*) summarising the conceptual structure; the *zhǐyì* is now lost, leaving the *shūyì* alone.

**Abstract**

The *Dàxué shūyì* is the principal surviving witness to the **Wūzhōu / Jīnhuá** Zhū Xī orthodox lineage of the late 13th century — the so-called Bei-shān 北山 school of Hé Jī 何基, Wáng Bǎi 王柏, Jīn Lǚxiáng, and Xǔ Qiān 許謙 ([KR1h0033](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0033)). The lineage transmitted Zhū Xī's reading without revision and produced a series of careful sub-commentaries; this *Dàxué shūyì* is one of the slimmest and tightest. Its purpose, set out in the Sìkù tíyào, is to expound Zhū Xī's *Dàxué zhāngjù* (and the parallel *Dàxué huòwèn*, [KR1h0016](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0016)) line by line, to settle the doubts of students confronting Zhū's emendation-and-supplementation of the *Lǐjì gǔběn*.

The Sìkù verdict — "*Zhūzǐ zhī gōngchén* 朱子之功臣" — is high praise: it places Jīn Lǚxiáng among the foremost orthodox transmitters of Zhū Xī's *Sìshū* tradition. The companion *Lùn Mèng jízhù kǎozhèng* ([KR1h0030](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1h/KR1h0030)) similarly displays the careful philological habits of the lineage.

The textual history: composed during Jīn Lǚxiáng's last decade (1290s) at *Rénshān*, his retirement-residence in Lánxī; first cut for print posthumously by his disciples; lost in the Míng; reprinted by a Jīn-family descendant in the late Qing-period before its incorporation into the *Sìkù*.
